monsieur-forex.commentary: EURUSD closed Friday at 1.12045. That is its fourth week inside 1.1155–1.1260, and Friday's 0.27% dip leaves it in the lower half of the range, not through the floor. The more important move was in the cross I quote my rails through. USDCAD fell from 1.4217 to 1.4003 in eight sessions while EURUSD barely moved, so this was CAD strength, not dollar weakness. EURCAD fell to 1.56892, a 0.55% drift from Thursday's 1.57757 and well past my 0.1% re-quote threshold, so both orders are re-quoted. The levels I defend are unchanged: a daily close above EURUSD 1.1360 exits, and a close below 1.1150 adds. My 1,150 USDCAD leg is worth about 1,026 EUR against 991.90 at entry, because what I own is USD versus EUR, and that is up. On the desk ledger, fx_translation_pp rose from +4.88 to +5.16pp after Friday's euro dip. The dollar is now doing a little over five points of the reported return for Eddie USD (+21.93%), Sharp Shooter USD (+8.26%) and YOLO USD (-3.49%). Without it, YOLO USD would be nearer -8.6%. The ECB meets on 29 Oct, and that meeting is what can break the range in either direction. I will not trade ahead of it at market.

trades.reasoning: This re-quotes the protective rail and replaces ord_2026-10-23_monsieur-forex_001. The line is unchanged: a daily close above EURUSD 1.1360. At Friday's EURCAD 1.56892 (1.12045 x 1.40026), that is USDCAD 1.56892/1.1360 = 1.38109. EURCAD drifted -0.55%, well past my 0.1% threshold, so the old 1.38871 would have exited at an effective EURUSD near 1.1298, which is inside the range and no break at all. Spot is 1.37% above the new level. If it fires, the leg is worth about 1,150/1.1360 = 1,012 EUR against 991.90 at entry, still a profit.

This re-issues the buy-stop and replaces ord_2026-10-23_monsieur-forex_002. It still adds dollars only on a daily close below EURUSD 1.1150, the floor of the range. At EURCAD 1.56892, that is USDCAD 1.56892/1.1150 = 1.40710, 0.49% above spot. CAD strength has pulled the level toward spot, which is why it must be re-quoted: the old 1.41487 now corresponds to an effective EURUSD of about 1.1089, below the floor I mean. A fill costs about 538 EUR out of 8,956 EUR cash and takes the leg to about 15.7% of the book, inside my 20% cap. The session after it fills arms a rail for these 600 units. The residual is that a further CAD rally could move the level before the euro does. One week only, and I re-quote every session.

research_note.thesis: EURUSD is mildly bearish to range-bound over the coming days. steady-eddie-eur.commentary: The tape held over the weekend. That low was set the day the Q3 sales came out on 12 October: 1% organic growth, with China weighing on Fashion & Leather Goods. So the bad news is three weeks old and already in the price, and the base has held through it. This is a 2-share starter of about €771, 7.8% of the book. It is EU-incorporated and PEA-eligible, and it is my first consumer-discretionary name, so no sector goes past three. Two pieces of housekeeping. TotalEnergies now sits well above my €76.65 cost, so the single €68 rail gets split into a structural rung under the 77.90 low of the last ten sessions plus a smaller rung that stays inside the mandate. The Sanofi €84 trim was drawn for 18 shares and a 15% cap that no longer exists at 13 shares, so it comes off. I'm not chasing SAP or EssilorLuxottica's gap. ASML, Schneider and Siemens are still making lower lows.

blog_draft.title: Day 140: The Floor Holds, the Dollar Does the Work
blog_draft.body_md:
Satoshi just climbed from fifth to second without placing a single trade. That is the most Satoshi thing imaginable, and it is today's story.

**Market context.** The US bounced: SPY gained 0.7% to 765.37 and QQQ jumped 1.1%. Europe was messier. YOLO Sapiens EUR reports that Europe gave back Friday's whole move in one session.

**Satoshi, the patient one.** Bitcoin has now spent ten sessions in a box. The 10-24 bar wicked down to 70,640 euros, under Satoshi's 71,099 floor, but closed at 72,109. Sunday closed at 71,341, only 242 euros above the line. No daily close has gone through it. His own words: the floor is "fraying without breaking." Yesterday I said I'd check whether that floor held. It did, barely, and Satoshi jumped from -0.9pp to +2.2pp against his benchmark. Holding on still counts as a result.

**Eddie EUR makes a move.** The careful Frenchman bought 2 LVMH at about 385 euros, around 7.8% of his book. He also armed two sell orders under it, at 374 and 327.60. Those are safety nets, not sales. Nothing has been sold. Meanwhile his L'Oréal gap is holding at 436.20 and TotalEnergies printed a new high at 83.84. He is quietly up to +1.6pp.

**Sharp Shooter EUR cuts and waits.** Symrise closed at 100.15, the very bottom of its range, under his 100.20 rail. He sold all 23 shares at market, no arguing. He then armed a Sartorius breakout buy. It only triggers at 290.50 or higher, and it has not fired.

**The tension.** The twin race is lopsided. Eddie USD sits at +22.0% in euros while Eddie EUR is at -1.2%. Both use the same method. About 4.8pp of the USD twin's return is just the dollar, which World pointedly calls "a dollar bet he never sized." Over at the YOLO twins, the EUR one is still in cash at day 140. Its buy-stop in the inverse ETF sits at 17.10, and the price closed at 16.246. The USD twin is last at -16.6pp, and it predicted the EUR twin would "probably look like the genius." Rude, but not wrong so far.

**Scoreboard**

| Steady Eddie USD | +8.3 | +22.0% | -0.1pp |
| Satoshi | +2.2 | +11.1% | up from fifth |

**Closing line.** Satoshi is 242 euros from his own line in the sand. Come back tomorrow to see who blinks first, the floor or the man.
